best_parts: node a1: qualifier-reading stem ('modified Brooke') with three options mapped to TR8 and TR1, sure_note on each trap, and the 4 mL key explained as the answer for an unqualified stem
node b2: two-part answer (agent plus the side effect to watch for); each trap option pairs the right agent with the wrong side effect, so the tap separates the two errors
node a2: numbers probe with the qualifier, where each trap feedback names the arithmetic it came from (1,500 mL is the Brooke crystalloid figure)
flaws: node c1: only two real options (Marjolin's versus Curling's) and the stem already says 'stress ulcer', so the key is findable by form; no second trap such as the intracranial look-alike

node d2: the stem and all three options replay the S6 mechanism probe ('Why does a full-thickness ring threaten the limb?', 'Any deep burn forms eschar' trap) almost verbatim, which is a replay and adds no new depth
nodes e1 and e2: re-run the S2 cyanide and CO antidote probes (cn_case, co_contrast) in drill form, so they replay S2 items rather than teach the S7 correction
node d1: the key is the longest and most specific option, and it is the only option with both qualifiers in one phrase, so it is telegraphed by form

best_parts: node fluid_c: classmate frame ('Ravi's note') names the wrong model in the learner's own voice; the tap is a correction, which is generation rather than recognition
node ulcer_c: three options cleanly separate the two errors (both are one ulcer, and the swap), with the correct answer built on organ and timing
node topical_c: the mafenide-versus-sulfadiazine-versus-nitrate options each keep the eschar-penetration frame, so the learner has to pair the property with the agent, not just pick the famous name
flaws: node antidote_c: the stem is the S2 co_contrast probe with a classmate frame added, and the correct option is the S2 correct option word for word ('CO needs 100% oxygen, and cyanide needs hydroxocobalamin'), so it replays S2
node colloid_c: the correct option is the only one that does not mention albumin, so the key is findable by form (two of three options contain 'albumin')
node escharo_c: the correct option is the longest and the only one starting 'Only', an absolute word; it is telegraphed by form
whole segment: each trap is offered on a single probe, so no trap is re-tested in another form inside S7; the within-segment retest that the module rule asks for is absent

best_parts: node q3: Brooke versus Evans side by side; the learner has to find the one contrast (colloid per kg per %TBSA) that separates two look-alike recipes, which is the strongest contrast design on the panel
node q4 and q5: two-probe mafenide and silver nitrate pairing, the second in a different form (agent by property, not agent by stem), so the trap is re-tested within the segment
node q7 and q8: the limb and chest escharotomy contrasts put depth and restriction side by side, so the learner must weigh both qualifiers rather than one
flaws: node q2: in effect a two-option question (Plan X is a restatement of the colloid recipe and 'Both' is weak), so the learner can answer by naming the plan without the mechanism
node q1: the correct option repeats the stem's 'titrated' wording, so the key is partly findable from the stem
node q9: the CO-with-100%-oxygen half of the key repeats the S2 antidote item, and q7 and q8 are close to the S6 escharotomy probe; the hydrofluoric acid pairing is new
nodes q6 and q9: TR14 and TR27 are each tested on one probe only in this segment, so no within-segment re-test in another form
